levels.label: 2-bit Dynamic (UD-IQ2_M / IQ2_XXS)
levels.summary: Uses importance-matrix vector codebooks and Unsloth Dynamic layer upcasting to fit giant MoE models (like 400B–750B) onto 256GB Unified Memory or multi-GPU rigs.
levels.whenToUse: Only recommended for massive Mixture-of-Experts (100B+–750B+) models where 4-bit won't fit. Avoid 2-bit on small 7B–14B dense models—just run a smaller model at Q4 instead.
levels.codingImpact: High sensitivity on small models: exact syntax, edge-case imports, and multi-file refactoring degrade noticeably unless running 300B+ MoE with Unsloth Dynamic UD-IQ2.

levels.label: 3-bit Dynamic (UD-Q3_K_XL / IQ3_M)
levels.summary: Squeezes 30B–33B dense models into 16GB VRAM or 70B–120B models into 48GB–64GB setups while keeping critical attention and router weights in 4–6 bit.
levels.whenToUse: When a model's 4-bit quant overflows your GPU by 2–4 GB and prevents fitting a usable 16K–32K context window.
levels.codingImpact: Moderate trade-off: algorithmic logic remains solid with Unsloth Dynamic (UD-Q3_K_XL), though subtle API recall and long-context code editing dip ~5–10% vs Q4.

levels.label: 4-bit Dynamic / K-Quant (UD-Q4_K_XL / Q4_K_M)
levels.summary: The universal gold standard for local AI. Retains ~97–99% of unquantized reasoning and coding capability while cutting memory footprint by over two-thirds and boosting token generation speed.
levels.whenToUse: Default choice for almost every local setup (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp). Prefer Unsloth Dynamic (UD-Q4_K_XL) or imatrix Q4_K_M whenever available.
levels.codingImpact: Near-baseline coding quality. Faster tokens/sec than Q8/BF16 (because LLM inference is memory-bandwidth bound), making agentic coding loops snappier.

levels.label: 6-bit Mixed Precision (Q6_K / UD-Q6_K_XL)
levels.summary: Virtually indistinguishable from full 16-bit weights in blind perplexity, math, and repository-level coding evaluations, while still saving ~40% VRAM vs BF16.
levels.whenToUse: When you have spare VRAM headroom (e.g., running a 12B–14B coder model on a 24GB GPU or a 27B–32B model on 32GB–48GB) and want zero quantization anxiety.
levels.codingImpact: Virtually zero loss on LiveCodeBench, SWE-bench, or strict JSON/tool-calling schemas.

levels.label: 8-bit Precision (Q8_0 / FP8)
levels.summary: Uniform 8-bit quantization (around 1.05 GB per billion parameters). Matches BF16 benchmark scores within statistical noise (<0.2% perplexity delta).
levels.whenToUse: Ideal for 4B–14B coding/reasoning models on 16GB–24GB cards, or FP8 serving on Ada/Blackwell NVIDIA GPUs via vLLM / SGLang.
levels.codingImpact: Identical to unquantized weights for code generation, regexes, and multi-step terminal agents, at ~2x slower tok/s than Q4 if bandwidth-limited.

levels.label: 16-bit Unquantized (BF16 / FP16)
levels.summary: Original training-precision weights (~2 GB per billion parameters before KV cache). Rarely needed for local inference unless fine-tuning (LoRA) or benchmarking reference accuracy.
levels.whenToUse: Research evaluation, LoRA fine-tuning baselines, or tiny ≤4B models where 8 GB of VRAM is trivial.
levels.codingImpact: 100% reference baseline, but consumes 3.4x the VRAM of Q4 and generates tokens ~2.5–3x slower on single-user local GPUs.

formats.name: Unsloth Dynamic GGUF (UD-*)
formats.tagline: Per-layer sensitivity-calibrated GGUF for maximum reasoning & coding retention
formats.hardwareTarget: NVIDIA, AMD, Intel Arc, Apple Silicon & CPU+GPU Hybrid
pros: Calibrated on 1.5M+ diverse tokens using KL-divergence sensitivity analysis
Keeps critical attention, MoE router, and output layers at 6–8 bit while compressing tolerant FFN layers
Substantially higher coding & tool-calling accuracy at 2-bit to 4-bit than uniform quants
cons: Slightly larger file size (~5–8%) than flat K-quants (e.g. UD-Q4_K_XL vs Q4_K_S)
Requires a reasonably up-to-date llama.cpp / Ollama build
formats.description: Instead of applying the same bit-width blindly to every tensor, Unsloth Dynamic 2.0/3.0 profiles each specific model architecture to protect sensitive reasoning and coding pathways.

formats.name: Standard GGUF (K-Quants & I-Quants)
formats.tagline: Universal single-file format powering the local AI ecosystem
pros: Runs everywhere—CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, ROCm, SYCL, and pure CPU
Supports seamless layer/expert offloading to System RAM when VRAM fills up
K-quants (Q4_K_M, Q5_K_M) are fast; I-quants (IQ4_XS, IQ3_M) use imatrix codebooks for tighter VRAM limits
cons: I-quants (IQ*) require slightly extra compute to dequantize on older CPUs/GPUs
Not optimized for high-concurrency multi-user batching compared to vLLM/AWQ
formats.description: Created by Georgi Gerganov and the ggml/llama.cpp community. K-quants group weights into super-blocks with mixed scales, while I-quants use non-linear lookup tables guided by an Importance Matrix (imatrix).

formats.name: EXL2 / EXL3 (ExLlamaV2 & V3)

pros: Supports exact fractional bitrates (e.g. 3.75 bpw, 4.25 bpw, 5.0 bpw) to fill a 16GB or 24GB card to the last megabyte
Fastest single-stream token generation and built-in Q4/FP8 KV cache quantization
EXL3 introduces lattice/QTIP-inspired quantization for dramatically sharper sub-4-bit retention
cons: NVIDIA CUDA focused—not meant for CPU offloading or AMD/Mac setups
Requires entire model + KV cache to reside inside GPU VRAM
formats.description: Designed specifically for enthusiasts running dedicated NVIDIA GPUs who want maximum tokens/second and exact control over weight + context memory budgets.

formats.name: AWQ & Native FP8

faqs.question: Why does a model use more VRAM than its GGUF file size on disk?
faqs.answer: Total GPU memory equals three parts: **Model Weights + KV Cache + Runtime/Display Overhead**. A 27B model at `UD-Q4_K_XL` might be ~16.8 GB on disk, plus ~2.2 GB for a 32K context KV cache, plus ~1.2 GB for CUDA compute buffers and Windows/desktop compositors—bringing real-world usage to ~20.2 GB. Our visualizer includes all three components automatically.

faqs.question: Why does coding quality drop faster than casual chat below 4-bit quantization?
faqs.answer: In casual prose, choosing a synonym ('quick' vs 'fast') goes unnoticed. In software engineering, a single flipped token preference can hallucinate a flag name, miss an off-by-one boundary, or break a multi-hunk diff patch. Benchmarks on LiveCodeBench and Aider show `Q4` (`UD-Q4_K_XL` / `Q4_K_M`) retains ~97% of BF16 coding accuracy, `Q6`/`Q8` is ~99%+, whereas dropping a small dense model to `Q2` can slash pass@1 coding rates by 15–25%.

faqs.question: How do Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models like 120B-A12B or 30B-A3B affect GPU requirements?
faqs.answer: MoE models decouple **capacity (VRAM)** from **compute speed (tokens/s)**. For example, `Qwen3-30B-A3B` has 30.5B total parameters, so **all 30.5B weights (~17.5 GB at Q4) must reside in memory**. However, only 3B parameters activate per token—meaning it generates tokens nearly as fast as a tiny 3B model! Even better: if an MoE exceeds your GPU VRAM, `llama.cpp` (`-ot exps=CPU`) and Unsloth can keep attention + shared layers on your GPU while offloading routed expert tensors to fast DDR5 System RAM.

faqs.question: What do Q4_K_M, IQ4_XS, and UD-Q4_K_XL actually mean in GGUF filenames?
faqs.answer:
• **`Q4_K_M` (K-Quant, Medium):** Block-wise 4-bit quantization where select attention/feed-forward tensors get 5–6 bits using fixed heuristics.
• **`IQ4_XS` (I-Quant, Extra Small):** Uses vector codebooks + an **Importance Matrix (`imatrix`)** measured on calibration text to pack weights tighter (~4.25 bpw) with better quality per byte.
• **`UD-Q4_K_XL` (Unsloth Dynamic):** Profiles KL-divergence sensitivity on every layer of that exact model over >1.5M tokens, dynamically promoting fragile reasoning/coding layers to 6–8 bits while keeping total size near standard Q4.

faqs.question: How can I fit a 64K or 128K coding context window without running out of VRAM?
faqs.answer: Enable **Flash Attention** and **KV Cache Quantization** (`Q8_0` KV cache). By default, engines store past token Keys & Values in 16-bit (`FP16`). Passing `--flash-attn -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` in `llama.cpp` (or enabling `Q8_0` KV Cache in LM Studio / Ollama `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0`) cuts context memory roughly **in half** with virtually zero measurable loss in coding accuracy. Avoid `Q4_0` KV cache on V-tensors for coding unless strictly necessary.

faqs.question: Should I buy discrete NVIDIA GPUs or an Apple Silicon Mac Studio for local LLMs?
faqs.answer:
It comes down to **Speed vs. Model Size**:
• **NVIDIA GPUs (RTX 3090 / 4090 / 5090):** Massive memory bandwidth (`1,008–1,792 GB/s`) and massive CUDA compute for fast prompt ingestion (reading big codebases in seconds) and blazing token generation—capped at 24–32 GB per card.
• **Apple Silicon Unified Memory (M3/M4 Max & Ultra, 64GB–512GB):** Lower memory bandwidth (`400–819 GB/s`) and slower long-prompt prefill on giant repos, *but* lets you load 70B–750B+ models silently in a 100W desktop box for a fraction of server GPU prices.

faqs.question: How are the Intelligence Score and Coding Score sourced and updated?
faqs.answer:
All data on this site lives in static, auditable JSON (`src/data/models.json`) curated manually without opaque live APIs:
• **Intelligence Score:** Sourced from the **Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5)** (which weights Knowledge Work, Coding, Science, and General Reasoning at 25% each; open-weight models peak up to `44` with Kimi K3, vs ~`59` for proprietary cloud frontier models).
• **Coding Score (0–100):** Overall local coding capability synthesized from benchmark evaluations on repository-level reasoning, code generation, and diff accuracy at `Q4`+ precision.
